updates.action: Co-led development of the Participant Outcomes Index with the strategy and product teams. Designed a holistic scoring methodology that integrated contribution rate adequacy, asset allocation appropriateness for age/risk profile, engagement level, and projected income replacement ratio. Grounded the methodology in academic research on retirement adequacy through a research partnership with Boston College. Built the data infrastructure to calculate the index consistently across the participant base. Created dashboards and insight narratives presenting the distribution of retirement readiness scores across segments. Incorporated the content into Plan Reviews and validated it with many of the top clients, with marketing and deployment planning still in progress.
updates.result: The Participant Outcomes Index was adopted as a core KPI at the executive and board level - recognized with the Ovation Award. Built, incorporated into Plan Reviews, and validated with clients, with marketing and deployment planning in progress. Generated thought leadership insights on retirement readiness that positioned Manulife as a genuine advocate for participant outcomes, not just an asset accumulator.
updates.impact: Participant Outcomes Index adopted at ELT level; Ovation Award 2025; content incorporated into Plan Reviews and validated with clients; deployment planning in progress
updates.full_story: The Participant Outcomes Index was the most philosophically ambitious project I worked on, because it required the organization to commit to an answer to a question it had been avoiding: what is the business actually here to do? If the answer is 'accumulate assets,' then AUM is your metric. If the answer is 'help participants retire with financial security,' then you need a different scorecard. Building the index forced that conversation, and it was a better conversation than most organizations have. The methodology work was hard - there's no universally agreed definition of retirement readiness, and the line between 'on track' and 'at risk' involves judgment calls. We worked through those judgment calls with academic rigor, in partnership with Boston College, and documented every assumption. Seeing it work was the exciting part: for the first time, we could see the distribution of retirement health across the participant base by segment, by employer, by region. The content went into Plan Reviews and we took it to many of our top clients for feedback. Marketing and deployment planning were still in progress when I left. The insights were sometimes uncomfortable. That was exactly the point.

The report itself has been referenced and shared more than two dozen times since its publication.

updates.action: Built plan review reporting on the GRID platform, benchmarking a sponsor's participant financial health against a stated comparison group including industry, state, or the full universe, using the Participant Outcome Index. Made it available on request through the sponsor portal or customizable through the relationship manager. Owned plan fit analysis, an inherited product where sponsors complete a survey of the design features they are considering and receive analysis of the projected impact, run through a SQL engine. Presented the Participant Outcome Index to selected clients for feedback and validation.
updates.full_story: Two products went outside the firm on the back of GRID. Plan review reporting let a sponsor benchmark their participants' financial health against whatever comparison group they named, their industry, their state, or the whole universe, using the Participant Outcome Index. Available on request through the sponsor portal or customized with their relationship manager. Plan fit analysis I inherited: a sponsor tells us which design features they are weighing, a survey feeds a SQL engine, and they get back the projected impact of the change. It was years from getting funded for an upgrade and it worked anyway. Both are advisory products delivered through an intermediary rather than software a client sits in unattended, and POI was shown to selected clients for feedback while I was there, with marketing and deployment planning still in progress. Worth being precise about that, because the distinction matters to anyone who has actually shipped external product.
